core.title: Cap acceptances at 5 per DESIRED OUTCOME; split the DESIRED OUTCOME when more are needed
core.given: A DESIRED OUTCOME and its acceptances in a plan.
core.when: The planner authors, revises or reviews the DESIRED OUTCOME or any of its acceptances.
core.then: Keep at most 5 acceptances per DESIRED OUTCOME; if more are needed, split the DESIRED OUTCOME into clearer outcomes instead of exceeding the cap.
prefer: Split an over-full DESIRED OUTCOME into several DESIRED OUTCOMES with clearer outcomes, each with <=5 acceptances.
Map each acceptance to exactly one test (acceptance_to_test 1:1); several tests may target one component (test_to_component N:1).
Give each acceptance exactly one metric_id.
Keep each DESIRED OUTCOME to one dimension and one lens_ref; acceptances inherit context from the parent DESIRED OUTCOME.
avoid: Exceeding 5 acceptances on a DESIRED OUTCOME, or gaming the cap by merging independent checks into one compound acceptance.
Acceptances with mixed measures (more than one metric_id).
One acceptance spread across several tests, or several acceptances sharing one test.
Mixing dimensions or lens_refs within one DESIRED OUTCOME.
core.why: A DESIRED OUTCOME needing more than five acceptances usually hides several outcomes; the cap keeps each DESIRED OUTCOME one clear outcome with one measure and one test per acceptance.
evidence: Count acceptances per parent DESIRED OUTCOME in the plan: every DESIRED OUTCOME has <=5.
Each acceptance references exactly one metric_id.
Each acceptance maps to exactly one test; tests may share a component (N:1).
Each DESIRED OUTCOME declares one dimension and one lens_ref; acceptances inherit context from it.
verification: Threshold: the per-WMBT ceiling on acceptances is 5; a count of acceptances grouped by parent DESIRED OUTCOME greater than 5 is a violation.
Ratios: acceptance_to_test 1:1 (one acceptance -> one test); test_to_component N:1.
Each acceptance maps to exactly one metric_id (no mixed measures).
DESIRED OUTCOME rules: one dimension and one lens_ref per DESIRED OUTCOME; acceptances inherit context from the parent DESIRED OUTCOME.
Scope: the over-cap count signals only the cap violation; the ratio, metric_id and dimension/lens/context checks apply to every DESIRED OUTCOME and acceptance regardless of count.
The cap signal needs a new observer: a counter of acceptances grouped by parent DESIRED OUTCOME over the changed plan artifacts; it is a violation signal, not an activation prerequisite.

facts.note: DESIRED OUTCOME and acceptance plan artifacts are identified by file kind and location; the profile supplies the concrete file kinds that play these plan-artifact kinds.
Fires on authoring, revising or reviewing any DESIRED OUTCOME or acceptance, including lists of five or fewer and edits to test mappings, metric_id, dimension, lens_ref or parent context.

values: acceptance count per DESIRED OUTCOME exceeds the cap
facts.note: Violation signal for the cap only, not an activation prerequisite; needs a counter of acceptances grouped by parent DESIRED OUTCOME in the changed plan artifacts.

fires: A planner adds a sixth acceptance to an existing DESIRED OUTCOME.
A planner drafts a new DESIRED OUTCOME whose outcome seems to require more than five acceptances.
A planner reviews or revises a DESIRED OUTCOME's acceptance list, even one with five or fewer acceptances.
A planner edits an existing acceptance's test mapping, metric_id, or the DESIRED OUTCOME's dimension, lens_ref or inherited context.
doesNotFire: Implementation or test-code changes that do not touch planning artifacts.
Editing documentation unrelated to DESIRED OUTCOMES or acceptances.

profileRequirements.meaning: The concrete plan-artifact kinds this rule applies to — the DESIRED OUTCOME grouping artifact and the acceptance item — so activation by file kind and the per-WMBT count check can identify which files are in scope.

bunOnly.reason: References the rule's term registry (term_id acceptance_cap, values.max = 5); the ceiling value itself is kept in the core's then and verification.

bunOnly.text: term acceptance_cap: the per-WMBT ceiling on acceptances; values.max = 5

neutralityNotes: This rule is content-level planning guidance: bun.json contains no stack, runtime, framework, language, package-manager, file-suffix or path reference, so the core is near-verbatim and imposes exactly the same obligation (cap 5 per DESIRED OUTCOME plus the co-retained ratio, single-metric, dimension/lens and context-inheritance checks; 'unless' is empty in the source and stays empty, so nothing was dropped). DESIRED OUTCOME, acceptance, test mapping, metric_id, dimension, lens_ref, component, product capability and the ratio tokens acceptance_to_test / test_to_component are ATDD plan-methodology terms shared across stacks, not stack specifics; they are kept, and the profile supplies only the concrete plan-artifact file kinds that play the desired outcome and acceptance kinds (bun.json states no plan-root or plan-item path, so no such key is claimed). The cap value 5 is the rule's own declared content (its term's values.max), not profile data; per-rule term and finding ids (acceptance_cap, acceptance_count_per_desired_outcome>5) are realization details kept in bunOnly while core verification describes the check generically. The over-cap counter is not yet observable (needs_new_observer): a realization must provide a counter of acceptances grouped by parent DESIRED OUTCOME over the changed plan artifacts.
